cohort: 94 patients with an unripe cervix (Bishop Score <6) near term, undergoing pre-induction cervical ripening in an outpatient setting.
finding: The double balloon catheter was superior to the osmotic dilator in cervical ripening (higher Bishop Score increase and greater cervical shortening), but patients using the osmotic dilator experienced less pain and higher satisfaction.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences in perinatal outcomes (which typically includes mode of birth) between the groups.
